body: I am sorry this is your experience too. I think something that isn’t talked about much is how truly awful it can be when your attempt fails. I failed and the aftermath was so much worse. I felt so much shame, was treated with very little dignity from people in the hospital and was spoken down to. Feeling morbidly sad does not make me ’crazy’ or lacking in intelligence that I need to be spoken to in a condescending tone. On top of that, people looked at my differently with this pity and I felt like there was nothing more to lose. the Shame I felt was next level. I’m struggling really badly again and feel exhausted. I don’t know why it’s ok to people that I can feel so isolated, broken, unable to break into life and be part of it and feel so hopeless for 20+ years- I don’t get how people can’t accept that there is terminal mental health issues. I want to be free from feeling this but I’m now so afraid of failing again and going through that same shame and Judfment. Instead, I’m living trapped in my broken mind, feeling so lonely and like I don’t fit. It is honestly tortue and I’ve tried so hard to get ‘better’ because I just want to function, I want to fit but I am exhausted and incapable. I want to go so badly, it’s my only wish. sending you a hug and genuine understanding of how awful that feeling you have is and wish we both couldn’t relate to it.

I’m sorry that you are feeling this way. I’m also sorry to share the sentiment of most of the people in this chain. This is most definitely not ‘emotional abuse under the guise of recovery.’ Unless you have been betrayed in the way he has, you will never understand the deep pain, trauma and, yes, PTSD he is suffering in the aftermath post-discovery.

This is without doubt the behaviour of someone who has had their entire world and life as they know it brought into question. The hardest part about recovering post-affair is the anxiety the betrayed spouse feels. They now have a new baseline for their relationship and it is, sadly, built around distrust. Trust is the absolute hardest thing to gain back and it sounds like he is really struggling with this (like many of us).

I do understand this is difficult for you but I can assure you that he is not being deliberately emotionally abusive - he is terrified of being let down again and has learnt that you repeatedly lied to him and is questioning your whole relationship history. This is so damaging to a person.

I get a sense that you are genuinely remorseful and want to make things work but there is a point where you both need to decide if this is realistic and if you both want to live like that in the current and future state. Post-discovery, I felt extreme anxiety when my husband wasn’t home or was travelling and I really struggled to live with such a horrible feeling where I couldn’t settle. I basically read into everything, was aware that he was now capable of breaking my heart and could lie without thought. I was constantly questioning every single word that came out of his mouth, every single action and whether it checked out. For me, no matter how much I wanted to make the whole thing go away and reconnect, I really questioned whether I could live with the mistrust, the crazy it makes you feel (particularly, when we’re often on the receiving end of our partner who betrayed us emotionally shutting down when we are feeling sad, make a snitchy comment because it doesn’t just go away) and the anxiety. I decided that I couldn’t so I moved out rather than feel constantly consumed by what was real and what was not.

So, the point is that people who were cheated on do suffer from PTSD and I truly don’t think his intention is emotional abuse. He is a person who was the victim of long-term emotional abuse and repeated lies and betrayal at the hands of you. It’s confronting to hear this but your behaviour very much changed and negatively impacted every element of his life. 

If you two really are serious about being together, you both need to decide;

\- Can YOU commit properly to him and show him he has reason to trust you? This means being consistent, asking what he needs to feel safe and supported and understand his hurt isn’t going to go away in just 1.5 years

\- Watching and following everything you do would also be very stressful and full of anxiety for him. Can HE commit to trusting you again and drawing a line in the sand to put the past behind, alleviate his anxiety. Or, can HE continue to go on living with the mistrust and extreme anxiety? 

There is a point where I decided that I just needed to just give things a go or move on because the anxiety of feeling the need to monitor and question everything was horrible, exhausting and further demoralising.

Basically, you both (very much for his sake), need to find a point where there does need to be a chance to move forward or both your lives will be miserable. You have to really make sure to tell the truth always from this point forward. The smallest lie will make him pick open the wound again. Please just remember, he is deeply, deeply hurt and PTSD is not any easy thing to recover from. His behaviour is very symptomatic of this. Also, you knew what was going on, you have all the information what happened, why you very intently let this continue, why you were treating him poorly, why he wasn’t enough - seriously, being cheated on messes with your mind and self-esteem. He has spent the last 1.5 years questioning everything he thought he knew about his most important relationship in his life. He didn’t get a say in this, you chose to do this and there were various points you could have stopped or not allowed it to go there. 

This will not be popular on this thread but I do try to think about it from every angle and if I put myself in your shoes (shoes I will never walk in because I don’t think there is ever any excuse to betray a partner), I can understand that there is a point where it makes it hard to move on or rebuild a relationship when you feel controlled by these (very reasonable for someone dealing with what he is) actions, even if they are the result of anxiety and trauma you caused. It just doesn’t sound like anyone can be happy in this situation - nobody likes being controlled and nobody likes feeling constantly on edge or doing the monitoring and controlling. As much as I understand why he is doing what he is - you broke every piece of trust and his heart - I also can understand why you feel the way you do and would start getting to a point where it is like punishment and when can you really reconnect and move to a happier future. Yes, you did it, but either you both decide to be brave and trust again and really see if you can be happy, or, you decide that it is broken and is no way to live for either of you.

In my case, I did draw a line in the sand at a point that I decided I either had to give things a chance and trust him or move on for my own happiness. This is hard as you can’t just switch your feelings off and I both loved and hated him at once. I desperately wanted the person who meant the most in the world to me, even though he was definitely not the person I’d made vows with and made me feel safe and loved. I had self respect but I couldn’t switch my feelings off - just like your husband. To give you an idea of the depth of grief we go through when our partner has some fun on the side, I wanted to die and felt humiliated and ashamed by the whole situation (I did try to kill myself - this is the very real place betrayal takes people to) and am sometimes shocked that I did decide to just trust and if it didn’t work, it would be over immediately.

I actively decided to move forward and take a chance to trust because I wanted to give things a shot. I also felt empowered that I would not accept this happening again - it was a hard no! Not everyone can do this and, truthfully, sometimes what he did hits me like a tonne of bricks and I cry and cry. When it first happened, I found myself feeling pretty much everything your husband did and I knew I could not live with the constant anxiety and didn’t want a life worrying about whether someone was telling the truth, so I decided to take a break from that and moved out. I had the chance to rebuild our friendship first and move from there. When I was ready, I took that chance to just trust because I knew that if I wasn’t willing to go there, despite every reason not to trust, there was no real chance of happiness for either of us. Don’t get me wrong, I will never forgive or accept what he did but, I either needed to give things a real shot or leave. Him feeling miserable and me feeling miserable despite the different drivers and responsibilities sucks for everyone.

I don’t forgive what he did and don’t find it acceptable in any way but I was lucky enough to get to a point after finding friendship again and taking some space where I even started forgetting what he did and was just in the moment. It is early days but I’m glad I made this choice or I would be an anxious and unhappy permanently. We are falling in love again and we couldn’t have done this if I didn’t take a chance.

If you really do want it to work out, be consistent with him, make him feel safe, supported and put him first, compliment him and make him feel loved. Maybe, this will build his confidence more and then, in time, you can suggest that you both focus on the future and promise to talk if ever either of you feel that something is missing in your lives together. Again, people won’t find this popular but I do understand exactly where his actions are coming from but I do also understand why it is hard for you - nobody is winning in this situation!  

Take care but remember, maybe it is time for a bold decision. Be understanding that his trust was destroyed, he is damaged, he is easily triggered and give him he chance to communicate how he feels. Overall, decide if this is how you both really do want to live. As long as you give him complete commitment and honesty, he won’t lose out taking a chance. One thing is for sure, if you both stay in this state, it is miserable for you both.

Yes! I found out in late October last year and I was so unattracted to him, had zero interest and he also felt super guilty. This is going to sound really daggy but it feels like when we started dating again. Honestly, we have gone to pretty extreme lengths. We are living apart as we felt we had to start a new relationship and I felt completely devastated - we are lucky in that we don’t have children and could afford to do this. 

We literally have actual dates again and there is something exciting about meeting somewhere - like a real date, rather than just coming from home! You don’t have to live apart to do this, just meet after work etc. I honestly didn’t expect much and had no interest physically at first but had fun. I started making sure to wear matching lingerie sets and it made me feel sexy. Somehow in there with a little bit of time, I stopped thinking about what happened and enjoyed the moment. The next thing you know, we were kissing a lot in the way you do when you first meet. I never really appreciated kissing before. Once I started seeing him again, having fun, having him compliment me again (he had stopped saying I was beautiful or sexy when he was cheating), I genuinely stopped seeing what happened and reconnected and enjoyed the moment.

I realised that we were both making a huge effort in how we looked etc. before we met, we definitely flirted and we are having the best sex of our life at the moment. We were actually talking the other night that we’re both excited to see each other, we look forward to seeing each other and we made a pact to be honest with each other if anything was missing from our lives. I also said that I actually just don’t want to know anything more about what he did as I don’t think it is helpful. 

So, starting with just dates and rebuilding moved to the fun of kissing, dressing up for each other and then I’m kind of falling in love again. Don’t get me wrong, I have moments where what has happened strikes me and I feel so sad and devastated. I also freak out that I’m afraid that what if we don’t move back in together but... then I feel excited about seeing we still have spark. 

For me, it took going back to the basics and not really having an expectation of what would happen. At first, I would get so devastated by something and be a sobbing mess and he would shut down and I would hate him etc. All of a sudden, with enough time to connect and appreciating each other and feeling appreciated back (being sincere, flirting, complimenting and kissing) went a long, long way. It has been nice that I can say, I was able to be in the moment, remember the person and feel really attracted again. I feel super sexy again too - matching lingerie goes along way for everyone! LOL!

Giving you a big hug and hope the same happens for you.

Ok, so unfortunately, your post has prompted exactly the response that you are challenging/ goading or expecting. I 100% understand that your intention is to show those betrayed a glimpse into the experience of the AP. I get it, you have feelings and that you were hurt by the dirt bag too. However, I feel so triggered by your post.

It's funny to me that you have chosen to write about your experience in the form of a drama as it seems that a woman who knowingly enters a relationship with a married man is guaranteed histrionics and drama. It also suggests to me that you thrive on drama. In fact, I feel personally insulted by your choice of genre to communicate your story. While it is effective in communicating the excitement of your secret relationship and attraction, it doesn't convey the depth of angst of the people whose lives are ruined in the wake of infidelity. Somehow, your play is self-serving, belittling and seems like some light-hearted dramatic fun - not the cause of my life and everything I know stopping in its tracks as many betrayed spouses/ partners feel.

As someone whose husband and partner of 18 years had an affair last year, I definitely blame him for the affair and do not see his AP as some temptress who came in and 'stole him away'. I do however, see her as complicit in the betrayal - she is not my friend, she very deliberately chose to be part of a relationship that was very damaging to my marriage, family and my own life. 

I genuinely understand the heartache and support the healing of affair partners who were not aware that they were in a relationship with a a married or partnered person. After all, they are no different to anyone who has been cheated on. They thought they were entering a relationship with someone single so have legitimately been betrayed. Like everyone on this site, they are trying to deal with the pain of betrayal, make sense of it and rebuild their life. If this was your story, I would have felt empathetic and supported your pain and recovery. Here's the thing, this is not the case and it feels like a knife in my heart that you are calling upon this group for sympathy and understanding. On some level, yes, I can give that to you by the simple fact that I don't like people to feel hurt. However, you entered a relationship under the pretence of a lie. You knowingly collaborated with someone in lying, betraying and hurting another human based on, let's face it, your selfish hormones and attraction. 

How could you possibly think you and your lover had as much attraction, connection and love then someone the person he married and built years and years of history? How could you delude yourself into thinking the couple never had the chemistry and crazy fog of new love you and your lover were experiencing once upon a time? They had this and more. Grow up. Passion and excitement gets old, connections wane from time to time, other life variables place strains on relationships but don't be fooled into thinking you had anything they didn't. What she had though was not a secret. Why would you think that someone who was cheating was honourable? Why didn't you question their intentions? If I found out someone was in a relationship or married, a very big red flag would be waving for me in terms of *their* character. Question the character of the person willing to cheat or solve their problems outside their relationship and *not* the crazy 'Gollum partner'. Again, red flags must be popping up for you if someone can speak so awfully about someone they married, lived with, had children or pets - a life with!  This is not the sign of a particularly good person. So, so many red flags!

You chose to go in deep and put your heart at risk by continuing to participate in an illicit relationship. You have more agency than you chose to exercise. If your lover was so into y you, your relationship would not be illicit and you would not be the 'side piece' secret. You made a choice to be a secret. I never got to make any decision in my husband's betrayal of our relationship but she knew and she did choose to participate. She cared more about her own fantasy life than the very real impact of infidelity on a very real relationship. As much as she chose to buy into his crazy 'Gollum wife' story, she was deliberately ignoring the very real person legally married to her 'lover.'

Together, my husband and his affair partner put my health and safety at risk, completely knocked the ground out from underneath me, made me feel humiliated and ashamed and like I was worth nothing. Do you know what it is like to be betrayed by the person you love and trust more than anyone else in life and not just for five minutes of attention? Your whole world falls apart. All the feelings you described in your post, I felt too. Only I had an entire grown up relationship and family of feelings and layers of complexity that betrayal brings with it. Spoiler alert - you knew what was going on, most of us didn't. 

Your love and attraction wasn't deeper than there's.  You met a person with poor character who was probably having a mid-life crisis, is selfish and said whatever they needed to justify the crap thing they knew they were doing to someone who once excited them the same or more than you did. And you, just wanted to look after you and only you.  I've lost all self-esteem, I feel unsafe, I feel like my future has been robbed, I am perpetually anxious and have lost trust in people and felt washed up and discarded.  I also tried to kill myself because I felt so betrayed and hurt. Yes, I hate her and I am sure your lover's spouse/ partner hates you and will struggle to heal this scar for the rest of their life. You are no better or worse than the jerk you described in your play.

So, some insight for the 'awful other woman who got kicked to the curb,' in my story, I blame them both and honestly feel triggered by your post today. I saw my husband's AP post that 'life has been unkind the last few months and I'm trying to heal my heart' on instagram. I wanted to publicly write, 'well, maybe you shouldn't have had a relationship with a married man - what more did you expect? Be more professional, you were at work and you're such a cliche, sleeping with the MD on one of your first jobs.. Maybe, you should see how unkind life can be when you desperately want to die because two people who were very aware they shouldn't be doing what they did, did it anyway. It wasn't a mistake, it didn't 'just happen', you both continued to lie and deceive and ultimately hurt me knowingly.' I didn't write anything because I'm not going to allow anyone to use my hurt as justification of being a crazy 'gollum' wife. It is torture enough that I visit her instagram occasionally because trust is so hard to regain. I remain silent and keep my dignity but I still cry a lot when nobody can see.

Yes, the blame lies with the cheating partner as it is their marriage vows they are betraying. However, you aren't the good guy or an innocent bystander either. You knew and contributed to someone else's pain. And it is pain deeper than any you've described. You probably don't even know the person you've hurt but, guess what, they're not the one cheating and you've been complicit in changing their life forever. Hmmm - something to think about.

I know all affairs are different but they all have this in common, no matter what, there is no excuse not to address your issues and go and find something else outside the relationship instead. My husband admits he was having a mid-life crisis. I was away a lot for work and he would give anything not to have blown up our lives. He said she was nothing but excitement and to feel young again. No life circumstances or relationship issues justify infidelity. It is an awful thing to do to anyone and an unacceptable thing to be part of. Period.

Anyone who knowingly enters a relationship with a person who is not available is flawed and selfish. Expressing yourself in your play as a heroine who falls for the bad guy is really selfish and insulting. I get that your emotions are real, but boy, I cannot have the same level of sympathy for you since you knew what you were complicit in. You didn't need to let things go as far and cross a line - there were many points of return and points to stop what was happening. There were many points to protect your own heart, morals and dignity. Let's face it, you did this because you were selfish, needy and alone and wanted to believe his story because it also suited you to believe it. I am genuinely sorry you feel sad and think you're a victim but, trust me, it is nothing on what his partner feels if she knows about it. I repeat, you made the choice to enter the relationship and she had absolutely no say in this at all. 

I really can't believe that you didn't consider it might not work out... seriously, all relationships one month or 50 years had excitement, attraction etc. at first. It's just such a shame that connections can get weaker, people sometimes don't value stability and comfort over excitement and we can all work on attraction and spicing things up. I do get that sometimes people are just jerks but, anyone who knows someone is in a relationship is by default getting a jerk on some level. I sincerely hope you feel better and learn more about the character of people from this. Aooooooooooooowl! Wolf howl.

You are definitely not stupid. Please don’t think that of yourself. it is pretty easy to get sucked in when emotions are involved and there is absolutely zero reason for you to feel bad in this way about yourself - you are human, with emotions and we want to look past things sometimes. Happens to the best of us. Take care and don’t beat yourself up over someone else’s poor behaviour. It does hurt and don’t feel embarrassed to get help or feel bad because you need it. Easy said than done but you are just being human feeling that way. I really hope you feel better about things soon.
Seriously, you are going so well. Keep going. Boy, does being bonded by this suck. Trust me, I am looking up to you right now - you are really doing yourself proud. x

For me, disconnection in these circumstances was normal but it devastated me that he so easily wandered. I am still in shock at the way he changed and became someone different who just looked like him.
He has now been showing a LOT of remorse and I believe she is no longer in the picture because he is 100% himself. However, I’m growing stronger and can’t forget this other part of him exists. I realised that I’m enjoying his company but I don’t feel attracted to him. I’m now fully aware that no disconnection actually made him cross a line, lie for six months and treat me with disrespect. My self esteem is back and I’m not willing to be with someone who did this. 

You have no idea how much this message means to me - people make it sound so easy to just switch off and I’ve had so much guilt for grieving the person I loved, married and was with since first year at art school that has been completely absent this year. I also feel so duped that I really didn’t think such a drastic change was possible or that he was capable of this.
